newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen weaker versus yen in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen weaker versus yen in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is likely to test lower against the yen in Asia on Monday after sliding below 115 yen in New York on Friday.
The U.S. currency, however, is likely to be well-supported versus the mark at around Friday's New York low of 1.7220 marks, dealers said.
"The dollar is likely to head lower versus the yen today. How far down would depend on whether support at 114 yen will hold or not," said a trust bank trader.
"If 114 yen does not hold, the dollar could slide to around 113.50 yen," he added.
Any recovery in the dollar/yen is likely to be limited at around 114.50 yen in the near-term as Japanese exporters are expected to be anxious to sell the dollar on strength, dealers said.
"After seeing the dollar's sharp slide in overseas markets Friday, some exporters may panic," said a trader at a long-term credit bank.
Meanwhile, the mark is likely to remain under downward pressure against the dollar and the yen amid lingering uncertainty about the future of a single European currency, dealers said.
Japanese institutional investors have been selling the German currency against the yen for hedging purposes. Such selling could increase this week, dealers said.
Tokyo operators will be carefully watching Monday's meeting of European Union finance ministers.
EU finance ministers who attended a dinner meeting on Sunday dismissed any talk of delaying the project.
"We will be carefully watching for EU ministers' remarks on EMU later today. We could see more swings depending on their comments," said the trust bank trader.
The dollar fell sharply against the mark on position adjustment on Friday in New York, after rising to a 39-month high of 1.7423 marks.
The U.S. currency closed at 114.33/43 yen and 1.7245.50 marks on Friday in New York.
